scope: Independent review of source-keys.png, design.png, revisions/keys-v3.png and source.json only. Four chronological sampled stills; no playback, timing, motion, or continuous-contact approval.

timed_key_evidence.source: Butterfly rests at the fingertips with a narrow, upright, near-closed wing silhouette and a low body at the contact area.
timed_key_evidence.candidate: Upright narrow lobed wing joins the small body above the foremost fingertip. Short legs extend from the body toward the adjacent fingertip contour; antennae remain attached. The internal diagonal gives a modest overlap cue.

timed_key_evidence.source: Hand is higher and the supported butterfly retains a similarly upright, nearly closed profile.
timed_key_evidence.candidate: Maintains the perched side view and attached body, wing, antennae and short legs, with a slight change to the wing edge and antenna posture. Fingertip support remains legible.

timed_key_evidence.source: Hand and butterfly have shifted left and lower; the wing silhouette remains steep and narrow above the fingertips.
timed_key_evidence.candidate: The hand and butterfly shift left and lower together. The narrow wing rises from the same supported body, and the leg strokes remain connected at the base.

timed_key_evidence.source: Butterfly remains perched, with the upright wing plane slightly changed in angle and its lower edge meeting the fingertip region.
timed_key_evidence.candidate: Preserves the upright near-closed silhouette with a small contour and posture change. Body, wing root and short legs stay visibly connected to the fingertip support region.

main_gap: No blocking gap in these sampled stills. The paired near-closed wings are compressed into one outer silhouette with a single internal overlap line, so the two planes are less explicit than in the photographed source.
observable_acceptance_condition: Met for the four supplied keys: each shows a recognizable sparse lobed-wing butterfly in a near-closed side view, with attached antennae, body and short legs, readable fingertip support, and modest posture differences. Continuous support and natural timing require playback and are outside this verdict.
protected_strengths: Sparse black-line treatment retains the selected design's lobed wing and antenna vocabulary through a side-view reconstruction.
Narrow upright wing presentation follows the perched source rather than becoming a broad frontal spread.
Small body and short legs stay attached to the wing root and fingertip support area in all four keys.
Hand and butterfly positions change together while the contact relationship stays readable.
